title: Deception-Probe Multi-Layer Ensembling Replicated on Small Models

original_idea.body:
# Deception-Probe Multi-Layer Ensembling Replicated on Small Models

**Problem:** A recent result found probe accuracy scales with model size and benefits from multi-layer ensembling, but the ensembling benefit was characterized on a particular model range and may not hold for the small models a beginner can run.

**Direction:** Replicate the multi-layer probe-ensembling experiment on a small open model (<=7B): fit single-layer probes at many depths and an ensemble across layers on a deception dataset, then measure the ensemble's AUC gain. Twist: test whether ensembling rescues small-model probes that individually perform near chance.

**Why it matters:** If multi-layer ensembling lets small, locally-runnable models reach useful probe accuracy, white-box monitoring becomes accessible without lab-scale models. Clean reproducibility on a single GPU.

**Relevant context:** 'Linear Probe Accuracy Scales with Model Size and Benefits from Multi-Layer Ensembling' (arXiv 2604.13386). 'Caught in the Act' (arXiv 2508.19505): 1.5B at chance, >7B 70-80%.
